cards.1: Go everywhere on the map with Cartography Sidequest and prove to the machine you surveyed every inch of your own cage.
cards.2: Reach the end of the Level Goal, and your reward is a slightly harder level.
cards.3: Find an exit to The Maze? Spoilers, there is no outside.
cards.4: It's All Upstairs From Here, so you ascend a tower to fight a guy who could have just met you in the lobby.
cards.5: Run or Die, so go that way and don't stop. The illusion of choice, accelerated.
cards.6: Escape Sequence runs you away from danger until you reach safety, and safety is a cutscene.
cards.7: Rise to the Challenge, climb up until you reach safety, and gravity is now a microtransaction.
cards.8: At the Broken Bridge you cannot pass until the developers finish coding the next zone.
cards.9: The Boss Battle monster exists solely to gatekeep your dopamine.
cards.10: In Kill Enemies to Open you are the janitor of death.
cards.11: Mass Monster-Slaughter kills many of the same monster, because repetitive labor is fun when it's violent!
cards.12: The pinnacle of heroic fetch quests is 20 Bear Asses for an NPC.
cards.13: The hitlist in Gotta Kill Them All is a psychopath's grocery run.
cards.14: A Kill Streak without getting hit is perfect for your anxiety!
cards.15: In Player Versus Environment the computer is controlling the game against you, and the house always wins.
cards.16: Player Versus Player is divide and conquer, so keep the plebs fighting each other.
cards.17: An Escort Mission with a suicidal AI is the ultimate test of your patience.
cards.18: Gotta Rescue Them All is just a hoarding pathology disguised as altruism.
cards.19: Stand in this circle and Hold the Line until we say you can leave.
cards.20: Save the Princess, who's been kidnapped again, and try better locks next time.
cards.21: On a Fetch Quest for an NPC you are an intern with a sword.
cards.22: Chain of Deals is bureaucracy as gameplay, so trade items for items for items.
cards.23: The Product Delivery Ordeal is Postmates, but with dragons.
cards.24: Collect the Plot Coupons to open the door, the narrative equivalent of a punch card.
cards.25: In Gotta Catch Them All, wildlife preservation is a hostage situation.
cards.26: On a Herding Mission the AI pathfinding is a joke we play on you.
cards.27: In the NPC Round-Up Mission you are wrangling digital toddlers.
cards.28: Live Items are living creatures you stuff into your infinite pocket, so don't think about the ethics.
cards.29: In a Companion-Specific Sidequest your ally's loyalty is bribed, because friendship is transactional.
cards.30: Complete your ally's Loyalty Mission, or they betray you at the finale.
cards.31: Love in the Romance Sidequest is simulated, so select dialogue option C to receive affection.
cards.32: A shiny hat is the Cosmetic Award that validates your hundred hours of meaningless grinding.
cards.33: Solve the Stock Video Game Puzzle, because the ancient architect loved pushing ice blocks around.
cards.34: A Mini-Game is a distraction game with its own rules, and pacing is a myth.
cards.35: With Variable Player Goals, why save the world when you could take photos of frogs?
cards.36: The Instant-Win Condition is a deus ex machina, so press X to end the simulation.
cards.37: For 100% Completion your digital grave requires all the shiny trinkets.
cards.38: In Gameplay Grading the machine judges your worth.
cards.39: Collect all the hidden rocks for the Secret Ending, and the true lore is disappointing.
cards.40: Your Bragging Rights Reward is an achievement that literally nobody else cares about.
cards.41: Normal misery wasn't enough, so you do a Challenge Run with optional restrictions.
cards.42: A Self-Imposed Challenge with your own restrictions is the Expert Edition of Stockholm Syndrome.
cards.43: With No Item Use for You, hoard the mega-elixirs until the credits roll.
cards.44: The No-Gear Level is a sudden, arbitrary strip search by the developers.
cards.45: A Speedrun skips the story and breaks the physics.
cards.46: Stepping on a twig in a Stealth-Based Mission is an instant fail.
cards.47: Time runs out in a Timed Mission, so the stress is artificial and so are the stakes.
cards.48: In a No-Damage Run one microscopic pixel of a hitbox ruins five hours of work.
cards.49: The Cake is a Lie and the reward was bait, so destroy the facility.
cards.50: Find the Princess in Another Castle, except your reward is a fungal hallucination.
cards.51: Players who Collect 12 Logs have tunnel vision and are forgetting how to actually play.
cards.52: Set your own goal of 100 Babies, and you are the architect of your own hell.
cards.53: Scoring Points does nothing, but you watch a digital integer increase and feel great.
cards.54: Repeat the same action until the bar is full, and the Experience Grind welcomes you to middle management.
cards.55: A Gold Sink is designed purely to delete the wealth you spent hours accumulating.
cards.56: The Hero Must Survive, so good thing you're not the hero.

cards.1: Flip a coin for The Rib-Breaker, and if heads, the fall breaks your ribs.
cards.2: The Youngest Brother has been losing, so the spirit of his father begins to mutiny against this servitude.
cards.3: The Tyrant Brother forces the boy to attack the strongest, and would as lief he break his neck as his finger.
cards.4: The Old Servant has lost his teeth in your service, so sacrifice him to fully heal another character.
cards.5: Whenever The Exile takes adversity from the environment, he finds books in running brooks.
cards.6: As a weasel sucks eggs, The Melancholy Sad-Sack sucks melancholy out of a song to restore his own ego.
cards.7: When The Weeping Stag is losing, his velvet friends abandon him, so sweep on, fat and greasy citizens.
cards.8: The Motley Fool confuses the enemy, so they must speak in rhymes, and wise men do foolishly.
cards.9: Ganymede switches strength and wit at will, a counterfeit man with a swashing and martial outside.
cards.10: Aliena is content to share the play with Ganymede, but she cannot go no further.
cards.11: The Shepherd earns gold as a true laborer, and he will eat what he earns and wear what he gets.
cards.12: The God of Marriage must make conclusion of these strange events, and the most pairs wins.
cards.13: Ill met by moonlight, The Fairy King is invisible and will overhear your conference.
cards.14: The Fairy Queen cannot attack any character as beautiful as an ass.
cards.15: The Hobgoblin will randomize the next attack, and Lord, what fools these targets are.
cards.16: The Changeling Boy causes a custody dispute, and she never had a sweeter changeling.
cards.17: The Ass-Head has the confidence, not the intelligence, so he is immune to insults.
cards.18: Read the prologue of The Carpenter aloud, and if you stumble, you played it like a child on a recorder.
cards.19: The Lion is no such thing, just a man with a gentle roar, as other men are.
cards.20: The Wall blocks all attacks, but through the chink poor souls are content to whisper.
cards.21: The more you spurn The Tall One, the more she buffs you, so use her but as your spaniel.
cards.22: The Short One is but little, but against the taller she is a fierce vixen.
cards.23: With The Purple Flower on sleeping eye-lids laid, you must defend the next played, regardless of team.
cards.24: When The Moon is waning, all magic will end, but the dog is my dog.
cards.25: The Bachelor deals paper bullets based on the words in your insult, and will live a bachelor.
cards.26: Swear you love The Lady Tongue and suffer the burn, because she had rather hear her dog bark at a crow.
cards.27: The Bastard creates a rumor that prevents two from teaming up, because he is a plain-dealing villain.
cards.28: The Drunkard will fabricate evidence of a vile encounter, but he has drunk to-day.
cards.29: The Constable can only succeed at the wrong task, O that he had been writ down an ass!
cards.30: The Headborough is a good old man, sir, who will support Dogberry and add confusion by talking.
cards.31: The Slandered Bride died defiled, but she does live, and returns fully healed.
cards.32: Let her be secretly kept in, and The Friar's Plan will convert slander into guilt on the attacker.
cards.33: With The Masked Ladies, which is which? I am your husband, if you like.
cards.34: The Penitent hangs an epitaph to mourn the death by slanderous tongues, and so gains attack.
cards.35: Benedick challenges Claudio to The Challenge and does not jest, so the loser loses the weapon.
cards.36: Born under The Dancing Star, you resolve the merry war if both players are smiling.
cards.37: Peace? The Prince of Cats hates the word, so attack him and he will strike back instantly.
cards.38: Kill The Joker and you shall find him a grave man with a plague on all houses.
cards.39: The Peacemaker will part fools and their swords, but you know not what you do.
cards.40: You bite your thumb at us, sir? Then you must attack The Thumb-Biter in a civil brawl.
cards.41: With The Lover it is either double or kill self, because he is fortune's fool!
cards.42: It is too rash and too sudden, so The Saint will accelerate the game timer.
cards.43: The Nurse will delay delivery of the message, and Lord, how her head aches!
cards.44: On The Rope Ladder you sneak into the enemy base without fighting, and the drudge toils in your delight.
cards.45: Buy instant death poison from The Apothecary, because his poverty, but not his will, consents.
cards.46: With The Sleeping Potion you appear dead, no warmth, no breath, until you wake up.
cards.47: The Happy Dagger is happy, because this is its sheath, and there it will rust.
cards.48: The Golden Statues end the game in a glooming peace where nobody wins and everyone feels sad.
cards.55: The Mask is a mistaken identity, so a targeted attack will redirect to the adjacent.

cards.5: Not for art, The Bone Flute was a remote control for the human heart.
cards.6: The War Drum was the state before the state, because when hearts beat together, boundaries dissolve.
cards.7: As a musician The Shaman did not entertain, but managed the tribe's reality.
cards.8: Control The Echo, and your repetition of truth will define the boundaries of the world.
cards.9: Gregorian Chant allowed no harmony, because harmony implies more than one perspective.
cards.10: Banned for centuries, The Tritonus is the Devil in music, because tension is dangerous.
cards.11: The Pipe Organ was the most expensive machine, with the voice of God and the budget of the State.
cards.12: In Hildegard's Vision the only way to break the rules was to claim God wrote them.
cards.13: The Fugue is not a song but dialectical logic, a trap where voices invert and combine.
cards.14: The Deaf Composer is proof that music lives in mental architecture, not sound.
cards.15: Before the character even speaks, The Leitmotif tells you exactly how to feel.
cards.16: In Bayreuth they dim the lights and hide the orchestra, so the audience does not observe but is absorbed.
cards.17: At The Crossroads the deal is real, even if the Devil is a metaphor.
cards.18: For The 27 Club the pattern is the point, and the gifts consume the vessel that carries them.
cards.19: The 12-Bar Loop will repeat, not from laziness, but from the insistence that the suffering is real.
cards.20: Why does The Blue Note hurt when it should not work? Because it is true.
cards.21: The Turned Back played for the music, not them, and if they did not get it, that was their problem.
cards.22: Love Supreme is a spiritual practice using the saxophone as a prayer wheel.
cards.23: The Improviser has to be ahead of his own understanding, because comfortable is wrong.
cards.24: The Session is a collective mind with no rehearsal, and discovery happens in the gaps.
cards.25: Payola is illegal when you bribe a DJ, but legal when you buy a playlist.
cards.26: The Teen Idol carries the music without carrying the threat, because safe and pretty is profitable.
cards.27: The Cover Version will sanitize the raw emotion for a broader market and keep the money.
cards.28: Play it on the TOP 40 until they like it, because familiarity breeds purchase.
cards.29: The Amen Break built entire genres in an infinite loop, and the drummer died broke.
cards.30: Is The Sampler theft? No, it is collage, because the Bronx used the past as a brickyard.
cards.31: The Crate Digger will unearth the break that everyone else walked past.
cards.32: The law did not evolve to protect artists, so Copyright Bot will protect the owners of the catalog.
cards.33: The Algorithm does not care what you like, only what you won't skip, and that leads to sameness.
cards.34: In the Loudness War everything is loud, so nothing is urgent.
cards.35: Just keep the vibe steady, because on The Playlist the artist is irrelevant.
cards.36: The goal of Retention Rate is to keep you here, mildly satisfied, forever.
cards.37: Some say 440 Hz creates subtle psychological dissonance, a frequency for workers, not dreamers.
cards.38: Maybe 432 Hz is the vibration of the universe, maybe a placebo, but it feels slower.
cards.39: Rock stars in Laurel Canyon with fathers in military intelligence? Just a coincidence, surely.
cards.40: Backmasking is a hidden command the subconscious hears, or maybe just noise, so do it.
cards.41: He worked from The Hospital Bed until the end, ignored by the industry and canonized by the culture.
cards.42: She did not change the notes, she changed the subject, and The Respect was suddenly a demand.
cards.43: For The Chameleon the mask is the self, so kill the character before they get bored.
cards.44: In The Silence the music is the coughing of the audience.

cards.1: Follow The Kayfabe-Money to the Trillions, and the Official Narrative is instantly out of play.
cards.2: Rule One for detectives is Follow the Money, because it determines how we proceed with our investigation.
cards.3: The Coincidence Engine declares any systemic anomaly a random fluke, if it was a coincidence.
cards.4: Any investigation has to go through Treasury's Ten Veils before it gets to the real Source.
cards.5: With The Privatized Towers you control the highest value asset for a fraction of the cost.
cards.6: With The Fourteen Million Bridge of their own money, the investors control a multi-billion dollar empire.
cards.7: The Double-Trouble Policy doubles your coverage, and if disaster strikes, you claim it happened twice.
cards.8: With The Secret Kickback your initial equity is refunded, and the profit is billions and counting.
cards.10: Silver Stream E-Link executes massive paperless transactions unseen by any other entity on Earth.
cards.11: Confront The 10M Anomalies and they urge you to mind your own business.
cards.13: Convar Data Recovery retrieved the impossible data, then could not give you any additional information.
cards.14: During The 40-Minute Window the computers were externally taken over to purge data.
cards.15: The illicit mega-trades could just be The Absolute Shopping Binge on a Tuesday morning.
cards.16: Before the dust settled, Paul Bremer's NBC Pivot had established the Official Enemy.
cards.17: The Put Options bet against the airlines, and in a single day the bet is millions.
cards.18: Buy The Raytheon Call right before a war starts and cash in when the military deploys missiles.
cards.19: The Global Manhunt launches probes that mysteriously fizzle out when they hit US soil.
cards.20: Ask The CBOE Shredder for the documentary evidence and you are told the records were destroyed.
cards.21: In The Stratex Spike your stock doubles and the FBI ignores you, because you have no ties to terrorism.
cards.22: The Ritz-Carlton Meeting hosts the Carlyle Group for a private equity breakfast on the day of the attack.
cards.23: The put order was brokered by Buzzy Krongard's Brokerage, former firm of the CIA's Executive Director.
cards.24: In The San Diego Cash-Out a staffer cashed out the day before, and no agency ever investigated him.
cards.25: The SEC Investigation examines millions of transactions and concludes nothing happened.
cards.26: The Single Institutional Investor places the put options on an airline and gets a free pass.
cards.27: Academic Probability proves it beyond a statistical doubt and gets completely ignored by the government.
cards.28: The Commission Handwave declares the origin of the money of little practical significance.
cards.29: Ptech Enterprise Architecture monitors your entire system, so it can foresee problems or cause them.
cards.30: To prevent massive failures, JP Morgan sought The Next Generation Blueprint, which can also execute them.
cards.31: Gain The Keys to the Cyber Kingdom and the most protected servers in the world are yours.
cards.32: In The FAA Basement Interoperability Ptech finds the exact holes in the defense escalation process.
cards.33: In Vulgar Betrayal the agents seize terror funds and get permanently blocked by their own bosses.
cards.35: Sarmand Limited provides the seed capital that got Ptech off the ground and into the US government.
cards.36: Who provided founding loans for Ptech? BMI Real Estate, run by Ptech's own Chief Scientist.
cards.37: The Radical Chief Architect writes government software while mapping the blueprints of the US military.
cards.38: The FBI finally raids Ptech, but The Pre-Raid Warning was given weeks in advance.
cards.39: The day after a raid, Tom Ridge's Rubber Stamp declares the system perfectly safe.
cards.40: Thomas Kean's Wallet had a real estate transaction with BMI, and the Commission never looked into Ptech.
cards.41: Rumsfeld's Declaration declares war on the adversary closer to home, the Pentagon bureaucracy.
cards.42: The Trillion Cushion could not be properly accounted for, so make the entries up entirely.
cards.43: Care about a good job and The Whistleblower's Reward is your director asking why you care.
cards.44: Dov Zakheim's Ledger fails to untangle the financial snarl but gets a massive defense budget anyway.
cards.46: PNAC's white paper Rebuilding America's Defenses predicts exactly what you need to conquer the world.
cards.47: The transformation is likely a long one, absent The New Pearl Harbor.
cards.48: Because fear tends to register on people, The Fear Integration bypasses all political opposition.
cards.50: Where the missing trillions went is The Unproduceable Report, because the Army was unable to produce it.
cards.51: Thomas White's Enron Playbook runs the military's budget, and Enron is the largest accounting fraud.
cards.52: The Building Seven SEC Vault collapsed, wiping out the evidence on Enron and others.
cards.53: In The Trillion Benchmark the war on bureaucracy is highly successful at losing even more money.
cards.54: If money is missing at the end of the day, The Standard Operating Plug inputs a false number.
cards.55: Every month the Navy report was missing money, and every month it had Linda Woodford's Eraser.
cards.56: The Iraq Pocket Change lost in a war zone is more than most countries spend on defense in a year.
cards.57: Combine insurance, insider trading and military fraud, and The Ultimate Heist wins.
cards.58: The Suspects' Story asks the perpetrators to investigate themselves.
cards.59: From CBOE to Convar, The Destroyed Records always manage to disappear into the ether.
cards.60: They told you it changed everything, and in Uncle FrizzleBob's Verdict it made the house infinitely rich.

cards.1: The Monophonic Monastery limits you to one single melodic line, because tonality did not exist yet.
cards.2: Gregorian Chant hypnotized the arena until polyphony ruined everything.
cards.3: Thomas Tallis overbooked the ring with The 40-Part Motet, and clergymen found it impossibly chaotic.
cards.4: The Renaissance Patron will fund a secular madrigal distraction and buy off the referee.
cards.5: The Harpsichord was weaponized by the elite to pluck your nerves, until the piano replaced it.
cards.6: In Sonata Form you state a theme, develop it in the middle, and lazily restate it at the end.
cards.7: In The Concerto Duel spotlight-hungry performers tag in a solo instrument to dominate the orchestra.
cards.8: Common Time resets the match rhythm to an inescapable, predictable drudgery.
cards.9: Hold your submission lock indefinitely with The Sustaining Pedal and its unrelenting sustain.
cards.10: Atonality and Serialism remove the musical key entirely, so attacks cannot be blocked.
cards.11: Extended Technique is rule-breaking, so use the instrument as a blunt percussion weapon.
cards.12: The Darmstadt School lectures the crowd until they boo, because unlistenable is sheer elitist power.
cards.13: Haydn wrote so many good quartets that The String Quartet is an inescapable team assault on later composers.
cards.14: The Brass Quintet is built to maximize sheer sonic impact and blow out your eardrums.
cards.15: In The Piano Trio a violin, a cello and a piano strike simultaneously as a tightly knit assault unit.
cards.16: The Woodwind Cartel chokes you out with reeds, and adding a horn is the deception.
cards.17: Summon The Symphony Orchestra and remember, not all orchestral music is classical music!
cards.18: From the rafters an Ethereal Choir will elevate the perceived divine importance of a piece.
cards.19: The Cartoon Conductor battles the orchestra with frantic baton swings to force them into compliance.
cards.20: Dramatic Timpani interrupt any promo, so the audience knows a massive hit is coming.
cards.21: A counterpoint hold by Johann Sebastian Bach is relentless, inescapable and mathematically merciless.
cards.22: Everyone else was forced to follow the rules Joseph Haydn built, strictly in Sonata Form.
cards.23: With a massive chorus of hallelujah, G.F. Handel will prematurely declare your inevitable victory.
cards.24: Many musicologists now believe Bach did not compose Toccata and Fugue at all.
cards.25: Without looking, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart counters your finishing move perfectly.
cards.26: Trash talk? Ludwig van Beethoven ignores it entirely and attacks with pure Romantic fury.
cards.27: Fryderyk Chopin strikes the piano so blisteringly fast that the crowd is dazzled.
cards.28: With Impractical Musical Skills you do something incredibly difficult just to flex on the crowd.
cards.29: Richard Wagner extends the match for hours until you quit out of sheer exhaustion.
cards.30: In crowded concert halls Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky will fire actual live artillery.
cards.31: Franz Liszt incites a riot, and his swooning fans trample you.
cards.32: Orchestral Bombing drops the entire brass section on your head to underscore a dramatic moment.
cards.33: Play The Rite of Spring by Igor Stravinsky, and the furious audience attacks for you.
cards.34: John Cage and Minimalism do absolutely nothing for minutes, which is the absolute breaking point.
cards.35: George Gershwin tags in a jazz musician, which is highly illegal and highly profitable.
cards.36: Wedding music will recycle Pachelbel's Canon Progression infinitely without spending any energy.
cards.37: The genre inherently demands Gratuitous Italian and German, so scream your performance instructions.
cards.38: Pause the match for The Cadenza and improvise a completely unscripted way to glory.
cards.39: Play your Leitmotif and you break them mentally before you even enter the ring.
cards.40: Attack in Uncommon Time Signatures and they physically cannot time their counters.
cards.41: Ominous Latin Chanting drops the temperature in the arena instantly and signifies impending doom.
cards.42: With the Ominous Pipe Organ everyone in the room knows the heel has officially arrived.
cards.43: Nobs and snobs fill the front row at The Opera Tonight, solely to look cultured to their peers.
cards.44: Opera Means Drama, so with a tragic aria in Italian vibrato you weep uncontrollably.
cards.45: Classical Music is Boring, so put the audience to sleep, and the referee doesn't see your chair shot.
cards.46: True Art is Ancient, so it is immune to all modern attacks and anything recently composed.
cards.47: The copyright expired, so the Public Domain Soundtrack is a free buffet for cheap media producers.
cards.48: Historically Informed Performance demands painful, un-upgraded medieval equipment, for authenticity.
cards.49: Classical music refuses to compress in The Loudness War, ruining the pop-industry's compression tactics.
cards.50: While they debate if Rock is Authentic, Pop is Shallow, you sneak a pinfall.
cards.51: Rock me, Amadeus, because classical was just the pop of the past.
cards.52: With the Symphonic Metal Transition your electric guitar has an entire orchestra backing track.
cards.53: Name your finisher with a Work Info Title of genre, number, and key, and confuse them to death.
cards.54: The Recording Era will trap your performance on a wax cylinder and replay your defeat forever.
cards.55: The Living Composers prove the genre isn't dead, because John Williams is romantic to his very bones.
cards.56: The music is rigged, so declare yourself the winner with Uncle FrizzleBob's Master Score.

cards.1: Extract the wealth, rebrand it as a Scholarship, and that is Cecil's Diamond Trust.
cards.2: Conquering nations with armies is messy, so Milner's Round Table conquers them with advisory boards.
cards.4: Get too uppity about your own oil, and The Imperial New Hitler Cast labels you Worse Than Hitler.
cards.5: The Federal Reserve Spider creates assets from thin air, and its web devours all other assets.
cards.6: Why would BlackRock's Aladdin AI predict the future when it simply owns the companies that dictate it?
cards.7: The Five Star Slush Fund is the deepest, darkest rabbit hole, and it cannot be taxed, tracked or audited.
cards.8: Welcome to the algorithmic company store, where your money comes on The CBDC Leash with an expiration date.
cards.9: In The 21-Year Gaslight the wars were one massive imperial divorce with a halftime show.
cards.10: For the space race Operation Paperclip resurrects the War Criminal as a Valued Scientist.
cards.11: The Deep Underground Military Bases are just waiting for the surface world to finally destroy itself.
cards.12: The NATO Peacekeepers wear white, and the contractors wear Rolexes.
cards.13: Spymaster Reinhard Gehlen lost one war, so he decided to start another one that never ends.
cards.14: To keep people afraid of communists, the armies of Operation Gladio do the terrorizing themselves.
cards.15: USAID's Infrastructure is building bridges straight to regime changes and data vacuums.
cards.16: The Invention Secrecy Act confiscates your Innovation, because it is now a matter of national security.
cards.17: With Hoover's Dossier Diplomacy the FBI is a personal gossip column, and everyone in power owes him silence.
cards.19: In the digital age truth is optional, and Algorithmic Deepfake Extortion weaponizes your own face against you.
cards.20: When attacked, Roy Cohn's Legal Meatgrinder ignores all rules, screams louder and sues for damages.
cards.23: The Pharma Mafia ignores all penalties and simply pays a small fraction of its profits as a fine.
cards.24: Spraying bacteria over San Francisco, Project Sunshine and Sea-Spray treat citizens as lab rats.
cards.25: Gain-of-Function Roulette supercharges a nasty virus with taxpayer money, so what could possibly go wrong?
cards.29: In Operation Mockingbird you just recite the lines and declare it was your own idea.
cards.30: In AI Cognitive Warfare the battlefield is your neocortex, and independent thought is highly suspicious.
cards.32: The Twitter Files Drop reveals all hidden censorship, and chaos ensues, but nothing fundamentally changes.
cards.33: With Transhumanist Neuralink billionaires escape death, and the peasantry are cloud-connected meat-routers.
cards.34: Smart Dust Panopticon knows everything, always, and reports back to whoever holds the DARPA contract.
cards.35: With 5G and Blue Light Grids your TikToks load instantly.
cards.36: Under the Social Credit ESG Score your freedom is a revocable privilege.
cards.37: Klaus the Sleep Paralysis Demon wants you to own nothing and thank him for the privilege.
cards.40: Controlled Opposition absorbs all rebel energy and steers it into a harmless cul-de-sac.
cards.43: The Vatican Secret Archives are God's filing cabinet of controversy, from Galileo's trial to dictators.
cards.45: The Book of Enoch is a divine soap opera of fallen angels and giants, too edgy for the Bible.
cards.46: Long before AI scraped your data, The Akashic Records were Heaven's cloud storage system.
cards.47: The Suppressed Wizards generate unlimited free energy, and the Federal Reserve immediately attacks them.
cards.48: The CIA Gateway Process is government-approved astral projection, funded by your tax dollars.
cards.49: Admiral Byrd went South with Operation Highjump and found more than penguins.
cards.50: Mussolini recovered The Magenta UFO, the Vatican hid it, and the OSS stole it.
cards.51: Look up, notice Geoengineering and The Dimming in the sky, and you're just a crazy conspiracy theorist.
cards.52: The military sees Water-Air UAPs every day, but officially they are just weather balloons in the ocean.
cards.53: In this house we don't obey in our underwear, we resist in FrizzleBob's Freedom Bathrobe.
cards.54: If they won't declassify history, Deep State Streetwear will accessorize it ironically.
cards.55: With The Satire Sanity Shield laughter isn't just a coping mechanism, it's mental armor.
cards.56: For The Analog Anarchist real power is tactile, rowdy and unplugged from the algorithm.

cards.1: The Pond-Gazing Peacock would help, but he is busy existing as a visual masterpiece.
cards.2: No one spits like the Flexing Rooster, nature's special effect.
cards.3: The painting ages for the Portrait Poodle, so don't look in the attic.
cards.4: If the Selfie-Stick Swan didn't post it, did the forest really burn down?
cards.5: The Fog-Weaving Cuttlefish never said that, and if he did, you made him say it.
cards.6: The Mockingbird repeats your argument in a whiny voice, and you're just like your mother.
cards.7: The Lure-Light Anglerfish offers a gift, then swallows you whole in the dark.
cards.8: The Revisionist Owl has always been at war with Eastasia, and has always been the victim.
cards.9: To the Caped Eagle you are the real heroes, and he is just a god.
cards.10: Fame is fickle, but to the Plagiarist Magpie stolen shiny objects are forever.
cards.11: The Smile-Bot Dolphin just wants to be loved. Is that a crime? Yes, it is murder.
cards.12: The Medal-Heavy General won battles he wasn't even present for, and that is leadership.
cards.13: Sheep sired by the Legacy Lion have opinions, and they do not concern him.
cards.14: You'll never leave the Smothering Kangaroo, because it made sure you're too weak.
cards.15: The Wire-Hanger Persian gave you life, and you repay her with dirt?
cards.16: The Golden Child Ant sparkles, so why can't you be more like your brother?
cards.17: Look at the subtle off-white coloring on the Business Wolf's card. It's beautiful.
cards.18: To the Tech-Bro Ferret people are things, so he moves fast and breaks them.
cards.19: CC the Micromanager Queen on Reply All before you breathe.
cards.20: The Brand-Ambassador Cheetah has no pyramid scheme, just a trapezoid of opportunity!
cards.21: The Tantrum Hippo ordered the tea iced, so the jungle is ruined!
cards.22: Are you saying the Thin-Skinned Balloon Fish is puffy? You're all dead.
cards.23: The Spiteful Wasp does not want the honey, but just wants the flower to suffer.
cards.24: The Scream-Pillar silences all logic until you pay attention to him.
cards.25: Only the Gauntlet Gorilla has the will to act, and also wants a banana.
cards.26: The Note-Writing Rat will write a name and become the God of the new sewer.
cards.27: Without the Sun-King Scarab the day does not start, so worship the sphere!
cards.28: Nature is messy, so the Clockwork Kraken fixed it, and you're welcome.
cards.29: The Flying Monkey attacks for the Boss, who is really nice once you get to know him!
cards.30: The Doormat Turtle absorbs the abuse, so the Narcissist takes none.
cards.31: The Yes-Parrot is an echo chamber, and you're so right, sir!
cards.32: The Energy Vampire Bat does not drink blood, it drinks your will to live.
cards.33: The Magic Mirror is a validation loop where everyone else is trash.
cards.34: The top of The Pedestal is lonely, but the view of you ants is great.
cards.35: Feed the Black Hole Smartphone attention, because it is starving.
cards.36: The Crown of Thorns is fake, but look how much he suffers for you! Look at it!
cards.37: Go have fun, because the Cross-Bearing Donkey will just stay here and rot alone.
cards.38: The Bandaged Leech would apologize, but his condition is flaring up.
cards.39: The Grudging Camel will forgive, but never ever forget a grievance.
cards.40: The music swells for the Emo-Goth Raven, whose darkness is too deep for you to understand.
cards.41: For the Naked Mole Rat King it is not a draft, just the chill of pure excellence.
cards.42: King of Kings was the Shattered Visage, and the name implies heavy depreciation.
cards.43: Fill the hole of The Bottomless Pit, and it's never enough.
cards.44: The Ghost of Future Past is immune to the present, because it used to be big.
cards.45: Uncle FrizzleBob has scissors, so rules are for people who don't.
cards.46: The Grey Rock is so boring and uninteresting that the Narcissist loses interest and wanders off.
cards.47: The Truth Bomb is no, and no is a complete sentence.
cards.48: You win by not playing, and The Exit Door is the only winning move.

cards.1: The Rules Lawyer demands you cite a non-existent rule, and if you hesitate, your action fails.
cards.2: The Optimizer is trying to weaponize ambiguity, and nothing breaks faster.
cards.3: The Nervous Beginner asks if this is right, and confuses clarity for safety.
cards.4: In a helpful voice, the Authority Figure cancels a move that is too fun.
cards.5: The Panic is an internal scream, so you freeze until someone tells you it's okay.
cards.6: With The Crutch you cannot take an action until another player gives you permission.
cards.7: The Sweat cannot handle success without questioning it.
cards.8: When the table stalls, The Silence is a moment where players stop asking.
cards.9: Whoever asks how to win is The Lost Winner, because they have already lost.
cards.10: The Nonsense State defies logic but feels right, because Blödsinn is not a mistake.
cards.11: Nobody is right, so The Effective Move ignores a rule if the result is a better story.
cards.12: The Amnesia ignores the precedent, but the players do not.
cards.13: Esq's Tears instantly win the meta-argument about rules interpretation, so cry harder.
cards.14: If the table laughs, The Correct Nonsense may be correct.
cards.15: Everyone takes a deep breath at The Pressure Valve, and no game state changes.
cards.16: The Less Rules removes one constraint, so if you need more rules, use fewer.
cards.17: The Red Pen crosses out one word of the rule lists forever.
cards.18: The Final Draft is labeled final, and immediately contradicted.
cards.19: The Fake Stamp is fake approval, and that is validation.
cards.20: The Disclaimer is a pseudo-legal loophole, so claim you read the fine print.
cards.21: An Anti-Rule read aloud at The Table is a declaration, and no discussion is allowed.
cards.22: The Controlled Void replaces authority with nothing and narrates the gap.
cards.23: Everyone looks at you in The Shared Attention, instead of at correctness.
cards.24: If The Safety Rail makes you feel safer, ask yourself, safer from what?
cards.26: Bad Design is a critique, so claim this is bad design.
cards.27: When the table stalls, The Stall stands in the room like a smell.
cards.28: At The Rage Quit you stop trying to win and are now telling stories.
cards.29: The Compliance Aid is simple words only, for people who hate improvisation.
cards.30: The Safety Blanket protects players who need rules to feel safe from Blödsinn.
cards.31: The Ironic Poster does nothing, but it bothers someone.
cards.32: Stand up and explain your move like a CEO, because The Slide Deck is marketing.
cards.33: Point at the player who is actually leading the table, and the Hidden Power is exposed.
cards.34: Challenge a correct move with The Illusion, because there is no correct move.
cards.35: The Blame shifts the consequence to the Game Designer.
cards.36: In The Interpretation you decide what another player's card really means.
cards.37: The Pot Plant does nothing, just observes, and its silence is a valid move.
cards.38: The Bureaucrat demands you mime filling out a form before you play.
cards.39: The Alien Tourist remembers the current board state, and you may revert to it later.
cards.40: Uncle FrizzleBob will rip up this card and rewrite one rule for the rest of the game.
cards.41: Wear The Judge's Wig and you are in charge until you laugh.
cards.42: Catch someone optimizing with The Police Badge, then default to rule-lawyering.
cards.43: Explain the science of your move in The Lab Coat, and the table is encouraged to let you try.
cards.44: Ask for a rule clarification, and The Dunce Cap protects you from judgment.
cards.45: The Dead Author has no intent, so the rules mean whatever the group decides they mean.
cards.46: The Ambiguity is open to interpretation, and games collapse under it.
cards.47: Break a promise in The Social Contract for narrative effect.
cards.48: Pull The Emergency Handle immediately if it gets boring.
cards.49: The Mood Swing changes your mood to anxious.
cards.50: With The Skill Issue you forget the trained ability you rely on.
cards.51: When it tips, The Collapsed Quest collapses.
cards.52: The Story Breaker interrupts a story connection that feels forced.
cards.53: The game is over when everyone at the table is relaxed or confused, so Stay Fluffy.
cards.54: Shout Kayfabingo for no reason and you win the game instantly.
cards.55: The Strange Alertness is awareness, so be visibly uncomfortable.
cards.56: The End is when the group decides it is done, with no winner.

cards.1: Nietzsche was right, and The Cold Monster only exists to maintain its own power.
cards.2: In the Pluralism Simulator you throw the rascals out, and nothing changes.
cards.3: Mussolini called The Public-Private Parasite corporatism, and the technocrats call it a Partnership.
cards.4: The Bureaucratic Labyrinth cancels any action, citing missing paperwork.
cards.5: The Poverty Trap is a Ponzi scheme that works perfectly, while the elite double their fortunes.
cards.6: With Cloud Rent-Seeker you own nothing, just subscriptions and licenses for things you used to own.
cards.7: Battle rising taxes in The Inflation Incinerator, and your money is worthless now anyway.
cards.8: The Sustainability Shakedown records trillions in profits while lecturing you on your carbon footprint.
cards.9: The Infantilization Barrage melts traditional thought patterns into compliance.
cards.10: If the situation is explosive, any random minor action can be The Trigger Event for a global crisis.
cards.11: In the Civilian Proxy-Force the rich take the loot and the poor are sent to the front lines.
cards.12: A divided resistance is a defeated resistance, so The Spalt-Pilz sows discord.
cards.15: With MK-Mind Melter the CIA fed unsuspecting citizens LSD to break the human mind.
cards.16: In Operation Whitecoat the state tested anthrax and yellow fever on its own.
cards.17: For years The Syphilis Syringe intentionally withheld therapies for study purposes.
cards.18: The Nerve Gas Cloud tested sarin, mustard gas and VX on unwitting soldiers.
cards.19: The Fallout Pig had soldiers drive over radioactive barrels, just to see if the trucks offered protection.
cards.20: The Space Dose Test blasted sick children with radiation to see how much astronauts could survive.
cards.21: From the US to Sweden to Canada, The Eugenics Board legally erased the futures of women.
cards.25: The Algorithm Enforcer silences dissent before it can even be spoken.
cards.26: Centimeter by centimeter, The Digital ID Collar ends freedom.
cards.27: With The Surveillance Car your vehicles now spy on their drivers.
cards.28: Individual development is not included in The Numbed Consumer's off-the-rack life plan.
cards.29: At The Obedience Parade the masses rally around the flag, and critical questions equal treason.
cards.30: With The Burnout Badger the resistance is exactly where the state wants it, ground down and powerless.
cards.32: The Illusion of Safety is a fake defense wall that shatters the moment it is attacked.
cards.34: Heads are no longer chopped off, but washed, by The Smiling Despot.
cards.35: Philanthropy is the ultimate mask, so The Elite Philanthropist gives, then steals.
cards.36: The Crisis Architect starts a proxy war and enforces the Pax Americana at all costs.
cards.37: At The Tipping Point the grotesque excesses of power eventually choke on the power of the many.
cards.38: It is always the same process, first the bureaucracy, then the police state, then The Mistgabel Mob.
cards.39: In The Grand Awakening even the most conformist statist realizes the farce has nothing to do with reality.
cards.40: The Systemic Rot follows a phase of freedom with institutional decay, corruption and obscenities.
cards.41: Laugh at an attack, because The Weapon of Humor is the universal remedy for dark times.
cards.42: The Self-Sovereign is immune to Propaganda and can see right through the Ponzi scheme.
cards.43: Being against something is easy, but The Utopia Architect needs stories of a freely organized future.
cards.44: The Free Will Anomaly cannot be forced, and it fights for human free will against the Monster.
cards.48: Uncle FrizzleBob's Blessing ends the game in a tie, and everyone goes outside.

cards.4: The cosmic joke of Hilfe, ich bin ein Mensch is being wired for love in a society built for spreadsheets.
cards.5: Charles Darwin knew that cooperation is not the enemy of evolution but its main engine.
cards.6: For Lynn Margulis life conquered the globe not by combat but by microscopic networking.
cards.7: Even among pure egoists, Robert Axelrod's Tit for Tat cooperation wins the long game.
cards.8: In the Synthesis of The Evolution Matrix the Alpha Male myth is a statistical rounding error.
cards.9: For Joachim Bauer we are biologically designed for social resonance, and we literally feel what others feel.
cards.10: To Matthew Lieberman rejection activates the exact same brain regions as physical injury.
cards.11: To John Cacioppo chronic loneliness is a biological hunger signal for connection that destroys the immune system.
cards.12: We are feeling machines that occasionally think, as The Empathy Circuit synthesis reveals.
cards.13: Morality isn't trained into us by society, because for Michael Tomasello toddlers help before they can even speak.
cards.14: Ernst Fehr would rather burn his own resources than let the unfair walk away unpunished.
cards.15: For Frans de Waal empathy, consolation and justice aren't human inventions but ancient evolutionary inheritances.
cards.16: The Scales of Fairness synthesis is part nurturing hug, part spiteful rejection of the greedy.
cards.17: Adam Smith, the prophet of capitalism, actually believed in empathy, and history conveniently forgot.
cards.18: Gary Becker reduced all behavior to a cost-benefit analysis and built a perfect model of a sociopath.
cards.19: Rutger Bregman debunks the cynical myths, because deep down humanity is aggressively decent.
cards.20: The Egoism Autopsy synthesis disables a global economic system built for a species that does not exist.
cards.21: C. Daniel Batson does not just help to feel good, because genuine empathy compels action.
cards.22: For Felix Warneken we are born helpers, and toddlers drop everything to assist a stranger.
cards.23: Generosity triggers the same pleasure centers as food and sex in the brain of Jorge Moll.
cards.24: Selflessness is not a sacrifice but a dopamine hack, and The Generosity Loop synthesis doubles it.
cards.25: For Edward Deci, paying someone to do what they love is the fastest way to kill their passion.
cards.26: Huge financial bonuses reliably cause performance-destroying panic, so for Dan Ariely the rational market is a joke.
cards.27: For Bruno Frey a price tag on a civic duty destroys the moral desire to do it.
cards.28: Carrots and sticks are for donkeys, so The Motivation Spectrum synthesis strips all financial rewards.
cards.29: Shoshana Zuboff reveals that surveillance capitalism wants to predict your future and sell it.
cards.30: For Jean M. Twenge every screen-based artifact actively increases loneliness and anxiety.
cards.31: For Byung-Chul Han we are no longer exploited by cruel masters but are the cheerful architects of our own burnout.
cards.32: We pay a monthly subscription to stay inside the Skinner box of The Surveillance Cage synthesis.
cards.33: To Carol Dweck you are unfinished, and that is infinitely more powerful than being gifted.
cards.34: In the Pygmalion Effect of Robert Rosenthal our expectations of others literally alter their reality.
cards.35: Helplessness can be learned, but so can optimism, and to Martin Seligman hope is a muscle that must be violently exercised.
cards.36: The Reality Redraw synthesis has the reality-bending power of simply paying attention to the present.

cards.1: Every decade The Decennial Oracle summons itself to remind you that your favorite movie is trash.
cards.2: The Director's Cut steals all credit from the writer and crew, because it's about the process.
cards.3: The masses in The Herd Consensus demand the same comfortable myth they have already purchased.
cards.4: Under The Regional Bias every nation has a proven greatest film that no one outside has ever seen.
cards.5: Citizen Sled-Dog is the peak of human art, so for five decades you debate the meaning of a child's toy.
cards.6: The critics decided that Spiral Pigeon, a film about male obsession, was the new objective truth.
cards.7: Three hours of real-time kitchen chores in Potato-Peeling Poodle obliterate capitalist entertainment.
cards.8: In Bicycle-Thief Fox cinematic power comes from making you feel terrible about post-war poverty.
cards.9: Monolith Macaque upgrades your intelligence and alienates you from everyone else at the table.
cards.10: Tokyo Turtle Story achieves cinematic perfection by placing a camera off the floor and not moving it.
cards.11: Sacrifice your own to protect ungrateful peasants, and Seven Macaques grants immortal legendary status.
cards.12: Directors love nothing more than Octo-Auteur, a film about how hard it is to be a director.
cards.13: Wind-Blown Pig adjusts the past to suit Americans, and the myth is immune to critical re-evaluation.
cards.14: Forfeit your hand to Mafia Pug, or wake up with your favorite card destroyed.
cards.15: Every time you feel a shred of childhood nostalgia, Galactic Penguin extracts real-world currency.
cards.16: You weep over Sinking Hippo, an entirely avoidable tragedy built on teenage emotional labor.
cards.17: In Possessed Chihuahua weaponized Catholic guilt is the most effective mechanism for cinematic terror.
cards.18: Hard-Dying Hound reclassifies your peaceful holiday as an explosive combat zone. Yippee-ki-yay.
cards.19: Hot Saxophone Hyena gains immunity to critical logic by declaring nobody's perfect!
cards.20: Wooden Woodpecker tells a beautiful lie, so you believe in wishing stars while turning into a donkey.
cards.21: In Rules of the Game Rooster the upper class collapses in a misunderstanding over a romantic affair.
cards.22: Nosferatu Bat is an illegal rip-off of Dracula that survives even if a court orders it destroyed.
cards.23: Eisenstein invented modern film editing in Potemkin Pelican just to legitimize a state revolution.
cards.24: Look at raw, unscripted mechanical reality, because Camera-Eye Chameleon strips all narrative illusions.
cards.25: Stagecoach Stallion pushes you out of your territory for a heroic, highly sanitized origin myth.
cards.26: With Replicant Raccoon the scientists agreed that our most likely future is corporate dystopian depression.
cards.27: In Brokeback Bovine all combat is resolved through repressed longing and societal pressure.
cards.28: In Shawshank Seagull patience and a rock hammer conquer all systemic injustice, every Sunday afternoon.
cards.29: With Pather Panchali Tiger the West had to admit that cinema existed outside their bubble.
cards.30: No player may attack in Spring Town Panda. You can only sigh deeply and reflect on broken marriages.
cards.31: Housemaid Cat slowly poisons you from the inside while cleaning your house.
cards.32: In Hong Kong Action Dragon true brotherhood requires shooting people in slow motion.
cards.33: In Underdevelopment Iguana the bourgeois observe the outcome without ever taking responsibility for it.
cards.34: In Red Light Armadillo trash becomes gold and logic becomes an illegal move.
cards.35: Prisoner Llama exposes the extraction of labor, then destroys your most expensive capital-generating unit.
cards.36: In Pancho Villa Vulture everyone is revealed to be a flawed, violent opportunist.
cards.37: Hanging Rock Kangaroo leaves abruptly, because the continent simply eats people.
cards.38: The hobbit-filled New Zealand tourism myth is brutally shattered by Once Were Wombats.
cards.39: Orson Welles steals Third Man Bulldog with five minutes of screen time and a monologue about the Swiss.
cards.40: Destroy Holy Grail Parrot completely and it is only a flesh wound, so it continues to shout insults.
cards.41: Marketa Lazarova Lynx confuses you with non-linear poetry until you forfeit out of exhaustion.
cards.42: In Teddy Bear Boar you fill out a form in triplicate, and failure results in immediate arrest.
cards.43: You have nowhere to move, because Round-Up Wolf extracts power through geometric intimidation.
cards.44: Come and See Bear is the total, uncompromised destruction of the glorious war movie.
cards.45: Iranian Deer accidentally predicted an actual real-world revolution, and fueled it.
cards.46: Night Counting Camel steals artifacts from the ancient dead to sell for immediate, short-term survival.
cards.47: Halfon Hill Sloth ignores all combat and avoids authority through pure comedic incompetence.
cards.48: Pay a heavy toll to Dry Summer Tortoise, because controlling the water means controlling the myth.
cards.49: Phantom Carriage Reindeer extracts morality by threatening you with the Grim Reaper's Uber service.
cards.50: Out of stubborn, frozen spite, Unknown Moose refuses to die.
cards.51: Nature Puffin escapes sterile aging by merging with the mythological landscape.
cards.52: In Flickering Walrus violent gangsters are lovable, quirky neurotics who blow up their own resources.
cards.53: The Ballot Box Badger wins any tie-breaker with skewed demographics and self-selection. See? Bias!
cards.54: For The Retrospective Rat what was brilliant is boring, because they're erasing the past!
cards.55: The elites of The Genre Pigeonhole refuse to let aliens, ghosts, or laughter sit at the adult table.
cards.56: The Wikipedia Weasel nullifies any argument with subjective opinions disguised as objective data.

cards.9: Einschlagszone/Opfer – jede Pointe zielt auf die Toten

rules.rule: Kein Doppelpunkt, nie 'Titel: …'; Titel steht im Satz.
Ganze Sätze, kurz, Comic, Flow; keine Fragmente/Telegramm.
Keine Satzschablone über das Deck.
Nicht vorlesen; Aussage + Pointe der Karte.
Nur Kartenwörter + Grammatik, max. ein Fluff-o-lect-Wort.
Regelmechanik nie als Regel; Power im Tratsch-Rückfall nie.
Keine Klammern; Ziffern/Symbole ausschreiben oder weglassen.
Opener bettet ein: Opener + Zeile = ein Satz; nie lose Wörter, nie Ballast-Satz.
Kein Opener doppelt; Familienabstand >= 10; Frage/Behauptung wechseln.
Nur was der Hörer kennt (kein Asset-Wissen, keine Bildbeschreibung ohne Bild).
Absurd statt Klischee (kein Büro/HR/Sitcom).
Tonfall heikle Decks (9/11, Verschwörung, Therapie).
Lint/Gate-PASS ist kein Qualitätsbeweis.
Länge 50–100 Zeichen; Tratsch <=110, Song <=120.
<=70 % Zeilen mit Titel vorn; kein Folgewort nach Titel >25 %.
Kein Semikolon.
Kartentext: Set >=90 %, Song ~70–80 %.
PDF führt immer; JSON wird nachgezogen.
Tratsch-Rückfall ohne Triplet: Titel + gedruckte Lore + POOL-Opener, Power nie, 'roh' markiert.
Song = Best-of nach Dramaturgie, nie die ersten N.
Erst Probe (8–10 Zeilen) an Georg, dann skalieren.
Bühnen-Dialog: A = POOL-Opener + Triplet bzw. Titel (ein Satz); B = Social Call/Erwiderung + Nachlegen bzw. bereinigte Lore; Power nie.
Lore-Bereinigung im Rückfall: Klammern, Titel-/Versalien-Etiketten, Stat-/Power-Angaben, Doppelpunkte entfernen (lore_fallback.clean_lore).

rules: Je Karte ein festes Triplet; Abwechslung nur über den Opener.
into_title: Opener + Kartentitel bilden einen Satz. own_clause: eigener Satz mit Punkt oder Komma (nie Doppelpunkt, SSOT S1), dann die Karte. Nie zwei lose Wörter ohne Satz.
Kein Opener zweimal in einem Song/Dialog; Familienabstand >= 10 (V-280). Frage und Behauptung abwechseln.
Kartenpassung: 'I once met'/'My neighbour is' nur vor Personen/Figuren, 'Ever tasted' nur vor Essbarem, 'I found a' nur vor Objekt-/Textkarten, 'You played' nur vor spielbaren Karten.
Status: POOL = im Prüfskript freigegeben; alles andere sind Kandidaten bis zur Freigabe durch Georg/WS0.
